page: Microsoft Azure DC16es_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration based on Intel Xeon TDX processors running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a rated clock frequency of 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, accompanied by hardware acceleration extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for vectorized and matrix mathematical routines. System memory totals 64.0 GB of RAM, establishing a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation. No dedicated graphics accelerators are provisioned, and the instance includes no bundled local ephemeral storage, requiring remote Premium Storage disks for persistent filesystems.

In synthetic and real-world processing metrics, the instance demonstrates mid-tier, balanced execution speeds. Computational benchmarks show consistent middle-range performance, with stress-ng recording 1,771.16 on single-core and 14,092.2 on multi-core loads, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 23,118.53 and Geekbench single- and multi-core ratings of 1,944.0 and 11,137.0 respectively. Extended vector instruction sets perform steadily, reflected by a PassMark extended instructions score of 18,731.6. Conversely, the memory subsystem scores in the lower quartile with a PassMark memory result of 1,371.4, highlighting a potential bottleneck for memory-intensive operations despite stable Redis throughput at 18.44 million SET operations per second.

The DC16es_v6 offers a balanced compute-to-memory configuration without the overhead associated with specialized GPU hardware or integrated NVMe arrays. Given the lack of local storage, disk operations and expenditure depend entirely on attached managed storage. The instance aligns well with enterprise web application serving, backend microservices, moderate database workloads, and standard software compilation pipelines where Intel Xeon instruction sets are beneficial, but high local disk throughput is not strictly necessary.

It features 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 64.0 GB of system memory, and a 260 MB L3 cache, complemented by advanced hardware instructions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance contains no GPUs and omits bundled local storage, relying on external Premium Storage for disk operations. Benchmark results place both single-core and multi-core computational throughput solidly within mid-range percentiles, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,137.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 23,118.53, while PassMark memory metrics reflect lower-tier performance. Delivering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory distribution without local storage overhead, the DC16es_v6 functions effectively for general enterprise web serving, compilation tasks, containerized application environments, and middle-tier database operations.
